A *posting spell* is one posting's life on its board: when it went up, when it stopped being listed, and how we know.
`build_posting_spells()` turns weekly scrapes into one row per posting, and `summarize_posting_durations()` turns
those into median days listed. This vignette walks through the pieces on a toy panel.

```{r}
library(edjobs)
```

## The panel: one row per posting per run

A state reads its archives into a panel. The required columns are `Run_Date`, `Posting_ID`,
`Posting_Identity_Method`, `District`, `title`, `date_posted`, `url`, `Posting_Source` and `position`. Optional:
`Close_Date`, `Is_Feed`, `Posted_Approx`, `Bridgeable` and `Role_Hint`.

```{r}
row <- function(run, id, title, posted = "2026-09-01", method = "Source fallback: district + board + title + posted date",
                source = "applitrack.com/demo") {
  data.frame(Run_Date = as.Date(run), Posting_ID = id, Posting_Identity_Method = method, District = "Demo District",
             title = title, date_posted = posted, url = "https://www.applitrack.com/demo/onlineapp/", Posting_Source = source,
             position = "Teacher", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
panel <- rbind(
  row("2026-10-16", "fb-1", "Science Teacher"), row("2026-10-23", "fb-1", "Science Teacher"),
  row("2026-10-30", "applitrack:demo:9", "Science Teacher", method = "Stable per-posting ID"),   # board moved to job IDs
  row("2026-10-16", "fb-2", "Cook"),                                                           # gone after one run
  row("2026-10-16", "fb-3", "Substitute Teacher"), row("2026-10-23", "fb-3", "Substitute Teacher"),
  row("2026-10-30", "fb-3", "Substitute Teacher"))
```

## Identity across runs

The same posting can change ID: a board starts publishing per-posting links, or a parser fix fills in a posted date.
`bridge_posting_ids()` joins an earlier fallback-identified posting to the stable ID it carries later, when the
source, district, title and posted date match uniquely and the two are never listed in the same run. A new exact
posted date is a real repost and stays separate.

```{r}
bridged <- bridge_posting_ids(panel)
unique(bridged[, c("Posting_ID", "Bridged_From")])
```

## Endings, starts and flags

```{r}
spells <- build_posting_spells(bridged)
spells[, c("Title", "First_Seen", "Last_Seen", "Ending", "Start_Basis", "Left_Censored", "Evergreen", "In_Durations")]
```

- **Ending.** A posting last seen before the latest run "no longer listed" only when its source was healthy the
  next run (the coverage calendar, or, before the calendar starts, whether the district returned rows from that
  source). Otherwise the end is censored ("censored: source error", "... partial", "... moved boards", "... relisted
  next run"). SchoolSpring's own record (filled, canceled) and the posting's own page (`posting_status.csv`) can
  confirm or overrule an ending. `POSTING_SPELL_EVENTS` lists the endings that count.
- **Start.** The board's posted date when plausible (on or before the first sighting, at most 365 days earlier);
  otherwise the first sighting, which is *left-censored* when the posting was already up the first time we saw that
  board.
- **Out of durations.** Standing ads (`EVERGREEN_TITLE_PATTERN`, or posted over a year before we first saw them),
  pools (`POOL_TITLE_PATTERN`), frozen boards (`frozen_board_runs()`), same-title postings that can't be told apart,
  left-censored starts, and, if the state says so, statewide-feed rows. They stay in the table, flagged.

In the toy panel, "Cook" ended: it was gone on 10-23, when the board still returned rows (there is no calendar
here, so that is the "district returned rows" proxy). "Science Teacher" is one posting, still listed, under its new
ID. "Substitute Teacher" is a standing ad, kept in the table but out of durations. Every posting starts on its
board's posted date; one with no posted date, first seen in the board's first run, would be left-censored.

## A state's rules

What differs between states is a `spell_rules()` object, set once per segment:

```{r}
spell_rules()$shared_titles                                   # the default
mt_like <- spell_rules(feed_entity = "OPI statewide feed", feed_in_durations = FALSE, shared_titles = "all",
                       partial_min_previous = Inf, moved_boards = FALSE, left_censor_after_gap = FALSE)
identical(names(build_posting_spells(bridged, rules = mt_like)), POSTING_SPELL_COLUMNS)
```

Every rule set writes the same columns, `POSTING_SPELL_COLUMNS`, so the states' spells stack. Where MT's rules
still differ from the defaults, and what changing each would do, is measured in the workspace's
`claude-notes/2026-11-11_spells-convergence.md`.

## Durations

```{r}
summarize_posting_durations(spells)
```

`summarize_posting_durations()` fits a Kaplan-Meier curve with delayed entry (a posting first seen at age 60 days
is only at risk from day 60), over `In_Durations` spells, and reports a median only with at least `min_events`
endings (20 by default). Read the result as "days a posting stays listed", not time to fill: only SchoolSpring says
a posting was filled.

## The first-seen lookup

Many boards give no posted date. `first_seen_lookup()` writes, for each posting listed in the latest run, the first
run that found it, keyed the way the app shows postings (`first_seen_key()`: district, title, link), so the app can
show "On the board since at least ..." instead of a blank.
